key_insight: ALBI pairs LLM-generated logic programs with formal Prolog verification to solve inductive logic programming tasks through iterative refinement.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a generate-test-constrain pattern for combining flexible LLM proposals with executable symbolic checks.
method: Replace the LFF paradigm’s ASP-based hypothesis generator with an LLM guided by structured prompts.
Test candidate hypotheses in SWI-Prolog and use diagnostic feedback to refine them.
Anonymize predicate names to test robustness beyond surface-level semantic cues.
evidence_signal: Across 30 standard ILP benchmarks, all three tested LLMs achieved 100% success, matching Popper with 1.4–1.7 iterations on average; anonymization preserved success while increasing iterations by 1.36–1.67×.
watch_item: Results on 30 benchmarks do not establish scalability to larger logic programs, and iteration counts alone do not capture runtime or LLM cost.
paper_title: ALBI: LLM-Guided Inductive Logic Programming via Iterative Generate-Test-Constrain Refineme
